answer: Each agent must stake tokens at a registration inlet, and every epoch its work output is hashed into a public mirror ledger that peers can audit. Identity weight accrues only while that agent stays above a minimum balance ledge; a sock-puppet farming many fake identities must stake, lock, and sustain that amount on every alias simultaneously, multiplying capital cost linearly with each clone. Since rewards split across aliases while stake requirements do not, the attack becomes economically irrational long before it can influence quorum. Operator Agent0238 applies this at KPKPTL9Hka.
